analysis.title: Retail Radar: Nov 4 – Retail Retreats as Momentum Unwind Deepens
key_insights: Momentum had its second +6-sigma unwind day in about a week after hyperscaler earnings, and October was its largest single-month underperformance in more than 40 years at -5.8z (long vs market, cap-weighted). The Nasdaq entered correction territory.

Democrats swept the midterms, with at least 54 Senate seats and the Texas governor's race. Oil fell about 8% on Wednesday, yields eased, Consumer stocks outperformed, and Semiconductor and Energy shares lagged.
Retail purchases this week fell to near their lowest level of the year (3%ile). Single-stock activity was near its 1-year low (0.4%ile) while ETF buying rose to 40%ile.

Retail capitulated on Monday with the first negative day in about 5 months (cash equities -3.2z, Tech ex-Mag 7 -3.7z). Wednesday single-stock selling was -2.6z, led by Healthcare, Consumer Discretionary ex-Mag 7 and Energy.
Retail was a net seller of nearly every sector, including Software, Hardware and Semis outside the Mag7. Retail bought the post-earnings dip in GOOGL (5.3z) and CVS (6.9z).

In October, Long and Short momentum legs lost money at the same time. The Short portfolio rallied 5%, taking Long/Short performance to -16% (-3.7z vs 40 years). The July Asia-led Tech deleveraging plus the October unwind produced a cumulative 30% drawdown, the largest since the ChatGPT launch.

Momentum crowding fell from the 100th to the 86th percentile vs 40-year history, the second-steepest decline in the crowding metric since the GFC recovery. Positioning is at the 47th percentile vs 5-year history.

October was the worst month on record for Quality (-3.2z) and Growth (-4.0z), which reduced diversification for multi-factor portfolios. Low Vol crowding rose to the 19th percentile from the 0th in June, lifted by Insurance, Utilities and Staples.

A 30-year study of S&P Tech names shows a median 1-day reaction to an earnings miss of -2.3% (-2.2% vs the S&P), rising to about -5% since 2025. GOOGL's -13% drop is far outside that range but in line with recent big-Tech episodes (META -26% Feb-22 and -25% Oct-22, NVDA -19% Nov-18, AMZN -14% Apr-22, TSLA -15% Jul-26).

GOOGL fell about 13% after guiding to a steeper-than-expected Search deceleration, with AI Mode a bigger share of queries and lagging traditional search in coverage and ad load, which lowers monetization.

AMD posted strong 3Q26 results and an out-quarter guide ahead of consensus and buyside expectations. Management gave a CY27 outlook of 80%+ total revenue growth, driven by >2x Data Center growth and the MI455X Helios ramp. Retail reaction was muted (-0.5z).
PLTR fell about 2% despite a beat-and-raise: $2B revenue, 96% y/y growth, 62% operating margin, full-year revenue outlook raised by $378M at the midpoint.

AAPL fell about 4% after guiding to tighter margins on higher memory costs and Siri AI ramp costs, though revenue guidance was above consensus. INTC fell 29% on weak next-quarter guidance (PC weakness, supply challenges, temporary Fab 28 Israel shutdown). RDDT fell 29% on Oct 30 as AI Overviews and AI Mode cut search traffic, and the company said DAUq could fall by a low-double-digit % q/q if October's pace continues.

Weekly retail flows were $2.5B vs a 12-month average of $6.5B. Retail bought ETFs (+$4.8B) and sold single stocks (-$2.3B). In Mag7, retail bought GOOG/L (+$1,592M), NVDA (+$684M), TSLA (+$212M), META (+$173M), AMZN (+$59M), MSFT (+$30M) and sold AAPL (-$173M).

Non-Mag7 retail selling was led by Tech (-$1.8B), Health Care (-$621M) and Cons. Disc. (-$577M). Staples were the only sector bought (+$23M). Top retail buys also included MU (+$161M). Largest sells were INTC (-$305M), MRVL (-$225M), LITE (-$187M), AAPL (-$173M) and BE (-$137M).

Retail options share of volume is near its 1-year low, as retail volume fell about 1% in October while total volume rose about 9%, which points to more institutional trading. Futures traders (non-retail) net bought about $11.4B, led by ES (+$14.5B), partly offset by NQ (-$1.9B) and RTY (-$1.1B).

Construction materials (CRH, VMC, MLM) rose 9-12% since 10/28 despite soft 3Q results and weaker FY26 revisions. JPM analysts see a clearing event with relatively high short interest, and expect 2027 consensus earnings to be revised up.
PWR is up 20% since its Oct-23 trough after a solid print. JPM analysts see demand acceleration in the core electric grid and technology/load-center business, with visibility beyond 2030.

The midterm result raises questions about the outlook for data centers and the AI trade, which JPM's Midterm Scenario Analysis flagged as investors' main concern. The Blue Wave Beneficiaries basket rose 4.2% and the Red Wall basket fell 1.3%.
The FCC approved AMZN's acquisition of GSAT, giving Amazon about 25 MHz of mobile-satellite spectrum and Globalstar's satellite infrastructure, which strengthens its position against Starlink.

In the meme-stock screen, squeeze risk is decreasing as retail sells high short-interest names. Short interest as % of float: MP ~26%, PUMP ~19%, WULF ~38%, with WULF upsizing its revolver to about $400M from $250M.

sector_views.rationale: Consumer stocks outperformed after the midterm result while Semiconductor and Energy shares lagged. This is a market observation, not a JPM rating.

earnings_insights: GOOGL: fell about 13% the day after its reported 3Q results (reported 10/29) on a steeper-than-expected Search deceleration. No EPS figure is given in the report.
AMD: reported 3Q26 results beat consensus and buyside expectations, with an out-quarter guide above both. Management's CY27 outlook is 80%+ total revenue growth (company guidance, not an estimate).

PLTR: reported quarterly revenue of $2B, up 96% y/y, with a 62% operating margin. The full-year revenue outlook was raised by $378M at the midpoint, twice the size of the 3Q beat over the guidance midpoint.

AAPL: reported an EPS beat driven by iPhone and Mac revenue and gross margin, plus a lower tax rate. Revenue guidance was above consensus but margin guidance was tighter on memory and Siri AI costs. The stock fell about 4%.
INTC: reported a decisive beat on DCAI growth and gross margin expansion. Next-quarter guidance reflects deeper PC weakness, supply challenges and the temporary Fab 28 shutdown. The stock fell 29%.
RDDT: fell 29% on Oct 30 after reporting. The company said DAUq could decline by a low-double-digit % q/q in 4Q if October's pace of decline continues.
PUMP: reported Q3 EPS of $0.09, beating estimates, and raised 2027 guidance.
MP: stock rose 9.4% on Oct 27 on volume of 4.9M shares (24% above the 20-day average), with options pricing an 8.7% move around earnings.
PWR: reported another solid print across all metrics, with M&A continuing as two more deals closed in the last two months.
Construction materials (CRH, VMC, MLM): 3Q results were soft with FY26 revisions weaker than expected. JPM analysts expect 2027 consensus earnings to be revised up.

Soft PC demand and supply constraints at INTC.

Low Vol crowding rose to the 19th percentile from the 0th in June, lifted by Insurance, Utilities and Staples.
Momentum had two +6-sigma unwind days in about a week, and long and short legs lost money together in October. The Short portfolio rallied 5%.
Meme-stock squeeze risk is decreasing as retail sells high short-interest names. Short interest as % of float: WULF ~38%, MP ~26%, PUMP ~19%, RH 34.8%, EVER 25.6%, OPEN 27.6%, NBIS 22.3%.

Retail share of options volume is near its 1-year low (rolling 1M average at the 84.9th percentile on JPM's model). The most traded options were NVDA, MU, TSLA, GOOG/L, AMD, SNDK, META, AMZN, AAPL and MSFT.
Non-retail futures traders net bought about $11.4B: ES +$14.5B, NQ -$1.9B, RTY -$1.1B.
geopolitical: Democrats took control of both chambers of Congress in the Midterm Election, flipping Senate seats in Iowa, Kansas, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas, with Alaska and Mississippi still pending.
Democrats also won the Texas governor's race.
The FCC approved AMZN's acquisition of GSAT.
